passages.text: This section and other parts of this Form 10-K contain forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties. Our actual results may differ materially from the results discussed in the forward-looking statements. Factors that might cause such differences include, but are not limited to, those discussed below under the caption “Forward-Looking Statements” and also those in ITEM 1A. RISK FACTORS in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. The following discussion should be read in conjunction with the consolidated financial statements and notes thereto included elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Overview Ross Stores, Inc. operates two brands of off-price retail apparel and home fashion stores—Ross Dress for Less ® (“Ross”) and dd’s DISCOUNTS ® . Ross is the largest off-price apparel and home fashion chain in the United States, with 1,904 locations in 44 states, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico as of January 31, 2026. Ross offers first-quality, in-season, brand name and designer apparel, accessories, footwear, and home fashions for the entire family at savings of 20% to 60% off department and specialty store regular prices every day. We also operate 363 dd’s DISCOUNTS stores in 22 states as of January 31, 2026 that feature a more moderately-priced assortment of first-quality, in-season apparel, accessories, footwear, and home fashions for the entire family at savings of 20% to 70% off moderate department and discount store regular prices every day. Fiscal Years The fiscal years ended January 31, 2026, February 1, 2025, and February 3, 2024 are referred to as fiscal 2025, fiscal 2024, and fiscal 2023, respectively. Fiscal 2025 and 2024 were each 52-week years. Fiscal 2023 was a 53-week year. The discussion that follows relates to fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2024. Discussion of fiscal 2023 items and year-to-year comparisons between fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2023 that are not included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K can be found in Part II, Item 7. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for fiscal 2024. Fiscal 2025 Highlights Financial results for fiscal 2025 were as follows: • Sales were $22,751 million, compared to $21,129 million in fiscal 2024. • Comparable store sales increased 5%. • Operating income was $2,707 million, compared to $2,586 million in fiscal 2024. • Operating income as a percentage of sales was 11.9%, compared to 12.2% in fiscal 2024. • Net income was $2,145 million, compared to $2,091 million in fiscal 2024. • Diluted earnings per share were $6.61, compared to $6.32 in fiscal 2024. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: Our fiscal 2025 Annual Report on Form 10-K and information we provide in our Annual Report to Stockholders, press releases, and other investor communications, including those on our corporate website, may contain forward-looking statements with respect to anticipated future events, our projected future financial performance, operations, competitive position, and our planned growth, that are all subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those forward-looking statements and from our prior expectations and projections. Refer to Management’s Discussion and Analysis for a more complete identification and discussion of “Forward-Looking Statements.” Our financial condition, results of operations, cash flows, and the performance of our common stock may be adversely affected by a number of risk factors. Risks and uncertainties that apply to both Ross and dd’s DISCOUNTS include, without limitation, the following: MACROECONOMIC AND RETAIL INDUSTRY BUSINESS RISKS We are subject to impacts from changes in the macroeconomic environment, government regulation or policy, geopolitical conditions, and financial and credit markets. Continuing inflation, tariff increases (or threats of increases), potential supply chain disruptions, and other external events may have significant negative effects on our costs, and also on consumer confidence, shopping behavior, and spending, which may adversely affect our sales and profitability. Elevated inflation, rapidly changing and increased tariffs on goods imported into the United States, other government regulation or policy changes, geopolitical conflicts, bank failures, federal government shutdowns, public health crises (including pandemics), and other potential, adverse developments and related uncertainties, could reduce demand for our merchandise, disrupt our buying patterns, increase our cost of goods, create limits in merchandise availability, cause shipping delays and increase freight costs, decrease our inventory turnover, cause greater markdowns, and negatively affect our sales and margins. All of our stores are located in the United States and its territories, and while we directly import only a small portion of our merchandise, more than half of the goods we sell originate from China, so we are especially susceptible to changes in the U.S. economy and trade policy in the U.S. (particularly toward China). credit_strengths.text: Ross operates a large off-price retail platform with two brands, generating substantial revenue and operating income. The business produces consistent operating cash flow, which comfortably covers capital expenditure and funds shareholder returns. This scale and cash generation underpin a minimal indicative financial risk profile, with net cash exceeding reported debt.

The company maintains a net cash position, with cash and short-term investments exceeding interest-bearing debt. Gross leverage is well below the sector median, and interest coverage is exceptionally high, reflecting minimal reliance on borrowed funds. This provides significant financial flexibility and cushions against cyclical downturns.

key_risks.text: Ross is highly exposed to tariff increases and supply chain disruptions, as more than half of its merchandise originates from China. Elevated inflation and changing trade policy could raise costs, reduce consumer spending, and pressure margins. These external factors may adversely affect sales and profitability, as highlighted in the risk factors.

The debt maturity profile includes a significant portion due within the next twelve months, alongside later maturities. While the company has ample cash to cover these obligations, refinancing risk could arise if market conditions deteriorate. The debt structure is straightforward, but upcoming maturities require monitoring.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Operating cash flow and free cash flow provide strong coverage of debt obligations. The ratio of free cash flow to debt is well above sector norms, and interest coverage is exceptionally high. This indicates a robust capacity to service debt from internal resources, even under stress.

Liquidity is solid, with a current ratio above the sector median and a net cash position. The company generates sufficient cash to meet its near-term maturities without relying on external financing. However, shareholder distributions absorb a substantial portion of free cash flow, which could limit flexibility if cash flow declines.

overall_credit_view.text: Ross Stores presents a minimal credit risk profile, supported by net cash, high interest coverage, and consistent cash generation. The off-price retail model is resilient, but exposure to tariffs and consumer spending shifts warrants monitoring. The indicative financial risk profile is minimal, not a rating, and reflects strong balance sheet metrics.

We view the credit as stable, with ample capacity to absorb adverse conditions. Leverage is below sector medians, and free cash flow covers debt and shareholder returns. However, the company's reliance on imported goods and the competitive retail landscape pose medium-term risks. Continued monitoring of margin trends and inventory management is prudent.

credit_strengths.text: Ross經營一個大型的off-price零售平台，擁有兩個品牌，產生可觀的收入和營業利潤。該業務產生穩定的營運現金流，足以輕鬆覆蓋資本支出並為股東回報提供資金。這種規模和現金產生能力支撐了極低的指示性財務風險狀況，淨現金超過報告債務。
該公司維持淨現金狀況，現金和短期投資超過計息債務。總槓桿遠低於行業中位數，利息覆蓋率極高，反映對借入資金的依賴極低。這提供了顯著的財務靈活性，並能緩衝週期性低迷。

key_risks.text: Ross對關稅上調和供應鏈中斷高度暴露，因為其超過一半的商品來自中國。通脹加劇和貿易政策變化可能提高成本、減少消費者支出並對利潤率構成壓力。這些外部因素可能對銷售和盈利能力產生不利影響，正如風險因素中所強調。
債務到期結構包括未來十二個月內到期的重大部分，以及較晚的到期債務。雖然公司擁有充足現金覆蓋這些義務，但如果市場狀況惡化，可能出現再融資風險。債務結構簡單，但即將到期的債務需要監控。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 營運現金流和自由現金流為債務義務提供了強勁覆蓋。自由現金流與債務的比率遠高於行業標準，利息覆蓋率極高。這表明即使在壓力下，也有穩健的能力從內部資源償還債務。
流動性穩健，流動比率高於行業中位數，並處於淨現金狀況。公司產生足夠現金以滿足其近期到期債務，而無需依賴外部融資。然而，股東分派吸收了自由現金流的很大一部分，如果現金流下降，可能限制靈活性。

overall_credit_view.text: Ross Stores呈現極低的信用風險狀況，受到淨現金、高利息覆蓋率和穩定現金產生的支持。off-price零售模式具有韌性，但對關稅和消費者支出變化的暴露值得監控。指示性財務風險狀況為極低，並非評級，並反映強勁的資產負債表指標。
我們認為該信用狀況穩定，具有充足能力吸收不利條件。槓桿低於行業中位數，自由現金流覆蓋債務和股東回報。然而，公司對進口商品的依賴和競爭激烈的零售環境構成中期風險。持續監控利潤率趨勢和庫存管理是審慎之舉。
